title: Area & Perimeter
description: Finding the perimeter and area of rectangles, triangles and parallelograms, including compound shapes.

notes.heading: Perimeter
notes.body:
Perimeter is the total distance around the outside edge of a two-dimensional shape.

📌 Definition
The perimeter of a polygon is the sum of the lengths of all its sides.

$$P = \text{sum of all side lengths}$$

🔑 Key Concept
For a rectangle, opposite sides are equal. If the length is $l$ and the width is $w$:

$$P = 2l + 2w = 2(l+w)$$

For a square with side $s$:

$$P = 4s$$

💡 Worked Example
Find the perimeter of a rectangle with length $8\text{ cm}$ and width $3\text{ cm}$.

  Step 1: Add the two different side lengths
    $8 + 3 = 11\text{ cm}$

  Step 2: Double the total
    $P = 2 \times 11 = 22\text{ cm}$

  ✅ Check: $8+3+8+3 = 22\text{ cm}$ ✓

⚠️ Common Mistake
Forgetting to add every side, or using the same unit for area. Perimeter is a length, so it is measured in ordinary units such as cm, m or km.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Add every side once.
• Use the same unit for every measurement before adding.
• A quick estimate can catch missing sides in compound shapes.

notes.heading: Area of Rectangles and Squares
notes.body:
Area measures the amount of space inside a flat shape. We count it in square units.

📌 Definition
The area of a rectangle is found by multiplying its length by its width.

$$A = l \times w$$

A square has four equal sides of length $s$, so:

$$A = s^2$$

🔑 How it works
Imagine covering the shape with $1\text{ cm} \times 1\text{ cm}$ tiles. A rectangle $6\text{ cm}$ by $4\text{ cm}$ holds $6$ rows of $4$ tiles, so its area is $24\text{ cm}^2$.

💡 Worked Example
Find the area of a rectangle $7\text{ cm}$ long and $6\text{ cm}$ wide.

  Step 1: Write the formula
    $A = l \times w$

  Step 2: Substitute
    $A = 7 \times 6$

  Step 3: Calculate
    $A = 42\text{ cm}^2$

⚠️ Common Misconception
Confusing perimeter and area. Perimeter tells you the distance around the outside; area tells you the space inside. Area always uses square units such as $\text{cm}^2$ or $\text{m}^2$.

✅ Tip
If you are given the area and one side, rearrange: $l = A \div w$ and $w = A \div l$.

notes.heading: Area of a Triangle
notes.body:
Any triangle takes up exactly half the space of a rectangle (or parallelogram) with the same base and height.

📌 Definition
The area of a triangle is one half of its base multiplied by the perpendicular height.

$$A = \frac{1}{2} \times b \times h$$

🔑 Key Concept
The height $h$ must be measured at right angles (perpendicular) to the base. It is not necessarily one of the slanted sides.

💡 Worked Example 1
Find the area of a triangle with base $10\text{ cm}$ and perpendicular height $4\text{ cm}$.

  Step 1: Substitute into the formula
    $A = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 4$

  Step 2: Multiply
    $A = \frac{1}{2} \times 40 = 20$

  Step 3: State the units
    $A = 20\text{ cm}^2$

💡 Worked Example 2 — Finding a missing height
A triangle has area $24\text{ cm}^2$ and base $8\text{ cm}$. Find the perpendicular height.

  Step 1: Start with $A = \frac{1}{2}bh$
    $24 = \frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times h$

  Step 2: Simplify
    $24 = 4h$

  Step 3: Solve
    $h = 6\text{ cm}$

  ✅ Check: $\frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 6 = 24\text{ cm}^2$ ✓

⚠️ Common Mistake
Using a slanted side as the height. Always look for the right-angle between base and height.

notes.heading: Area of a Parallelogram
notes.body:
A parallelogram is a four-sided shape with two pairs of parallel sides. Its area rule looks like a stretched rectangle.

📌 Definition
The area of a parallelogram is its base multiplied by its perpendicular height.

$$A = b \times h$$

🔑 How it works
If you cut a right-angled triangle from one end of a parallelogram and slide it to the other side, it forms a rectangle with the same base and height. That is why the formula is $b \times h$, not $a \times b$ (where $a$ and $b$ are slanted sides).

💡 Worked Example 1
Find the area of a parallelogram with base $7\text{ cm}$ and perpendicular height $5\text{ cm}$.

  Step 1: Substitute
    $A = 7 \times 5$

  Step 2: Calculate
    $A = 35\text{ cm}^2$

💡 Worked Example 2 — Finding the height
A parallelogram has area $28\text{ cm}^2$ and base $7\text{ cm}$. Find the perpendicular height.

  Step 1: Use $A = b \times h$
    $28 = 7 \times h$

  Step 2: Divide both sides by 7
    $h = 4\text{ cm}$

📎 Key Points to Remember
• The height must be perpendicular to the chosen base.
• A rectangle is a special parallelogram, so the same formula works.
• Changing the slant of the sides does not change the area if the base and height stay the same.

notes.heading: Compound Shapes
notes.body:
A compound shape is made by joining two or more simple shapes together.

📌 Definition
To find the area of a compound shape, split it into simple parts (rectangles, triangles, parallelograms), find the area of each part, then add the results.

🔑 Key Concept
For the perimeter of a compound shape, only count the outside edges. Some lengths may be missing, but you can work them out from the other measurements.

💡 Worked Example — Area and perimeter of an L-shape
An L-shape is made from two rectangles: one $5\text{ cm}$ by $4\text{ cm}$ and another $3\text{ cm}$ by $2\text{ cm}$.

  Step 1: Area of first rectangle
    $A_1 = 5 \times 4 = 20\text{ cm}^2$

  Step 2: Area of second rectangle
    $A_2 = 3 \times 2 = 6\text{ cm}^2$

  Step 3: Total area
    $A = 20 + 6 = 26\text{ cm}^2$

  ✅ Tip: Draw the shape and label every side before calculating.

⚠️ Common Mistake
For area: adding side lengths instead of multiplying them for each part. For perimeter: counting an internal line that is not on the outside edge.

notes.heading: Units and Conversions
notes.body:
Measurements must be in the correct unit, and area units are different from length units.

📌 Definition
A square unit is a square whose sides are each one unit long. $1\text{ cm}^2$ is the area of a $1\text{ cm}$ by $1\text{ cm}$ square.

🔑 Key Concept — Converting area units
Because area is two-dimensional, converting between square units uses squares of the length conversion.

$$1\text{ m} = 100\text{ cm}$$

so

$$1\text{ m}^2 = 100 \times 100 = 10\,000\text{ cm}^2$$

Similarly:

$$1\text{ km}^2 = 1\,000\,000\text{ m}^2$$

💡 Worked Example
Convert $3\text{ m}^2$ into $\text{cm}^2$.

  Step 1: Use the conversion factor
    $1\text{ m}^2 = 10\,000\text{ cm}^2$

  Step 2: Multiply
    $3 \times 10\,000 = 30\,000\text{ cm}^2$

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Perimeter uses ordinary units: mm, cm, m, km.
• Area uses square units: $\text{mm}^2$, $\text{cm}^2$, $\text{m}^2$, $\text{km}^2$.
• Always convert measurements to the same unit before calculating area or perimeter.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Thinking $1\text{ m}^2 = 100\text{ cm}^2$. It is actually $10\,000\text{ cm}^2$ because the conversion applies in two directions.

notes.heading: Problem Solving and Checking
notes.body:
Many area and perimeter questions ask you to work backwards or solve a real-life problem.

🔑 Key Concept — Working backwards
If you know the area and one dimension, you can find the other:

$$\text{rectangle: } l = \frac{A}{w} \quad \text{and} \quad w = \frac{A}{l}$$

$$\text{triangle: } b = \frac{2A}{h} \quad \text{and} \quad h = \frac{2A}{b}$$

$$\text{parallelogram: } b = \frac{A}{h} \quad \text{and} \quad h = \frac{A}{b}$$

💡 Worked Example — Garden path
A rectangular garden is $12\text{ m}$ long and $8\text{ m}$ wide. A path $1\text{ m}$ wide runs all the way around the inside edge. Find the area of the path.

  Step 1: Area of whole garden
    $A_{\text{garden}} = 12 \times 8 = 96\text{ m}^2$

  Step 2: Dimensions of the inner flower bed
    Length: $12 - 1 - 1 = 10\text{ m}$
    Width: $8 - 1 - 1 = 6\text{ m}$

  Step 3: Area of inner bed
    $A_{\text{bed}} = 10 \times 6 = 60\text{ m}^2$

  Step 4: Area of path
    $A_{\text{path}} = 96 - 60 = 36\text{ m}^2$

✅ Check
Estimate: the path is about $1\text{ m}$ wide around a $12\text{ m}\times 8\text{ m}$ rectangle, so its area should be a bit less than the garden's perimeter ($40\text{ m}$) times $1\text{ m}$, giving about $36\text{ m}^2$. The answer is reasonable.

⚠️ Common Misconception
Subtracting only $1\text{ m}$ from each dimension when a border runs on both sides. Remember to subtract twice the border width.

flashcards.definition: The total distance around the outside of a 2D shape.
flashcards.example: A rectangle $8\text{ cm}$ by $3\text{ cm}$ has perimeter $8+3+8+3 = 22\text{ cm}$.

flashcards.definition: The amount of space inside a 2D shape, measured in square units.
flashcards.example: A $5\text{ cm}$ by $5\text{ cm}$ square has area $25\text{ cm}^2$.

flashcards.definition: Area equals length multiplied by width: $A = l \times w$.
flashcards.example: Length $8\text{ cm}$ and width $3\text{ cm}$ gives area $24\text{ cm}^2$.

flashcards.definition: Area equals side length squared: $A = s^2$.
flashcards.example: A square with side $6\text{ cm}$ has area $36\text{ cm}^2$.

flashcards.definition: Area equals one half of base multiplied by perpendicular height: $A = \frac{1}{2}bh$.
flashcards.example: Base $12\text{ cm}$ and height $5\text{ cm}$ gives area $30\text{ cm}^2$.

flashcards.definition: Area equals base multiplied by perpendicular height: $A = b \times h$.
flashcards.example: Base $9\text{ cm}$ and height $4\text{ cm}$ gives area $36\text{ cm}^2$.

flashcards.definition: The straight-up distance from the base to the opposite point, measured at 90 degrees.
flashcards.example: In a triangle, the height is not a slanted side unless it meets the base at a right angle.

flashcards.definition: A shape made by combining two or more simpler shapes.
flashcards.example: An L-shape can be split into two rectangles; find each area and add them.

flashcards.definition: Units used for area, written with a small 2 after the unit symbol.
flashcards.example: $\text{cm}^2$ means square centimetres and $\text{m}^2$ means square metres.

flashcards.definition: Rearrange the area formula to find an unknown length.
flashcards.example: If a rectangle has area $48\text{ cm}^2$ and length $8\text{ cm}$, its width is $48 \div 8 = 6\text{ cm}$.

flashcards.definition: Converting square units uses the square of the length conversion factor.
Add only the outside edges of the whole shape.
flashcards.example: For an L-shape, do not count the internal line where the two rectangles meet.

questions.stem: What is the perimeter of a rectangle with length $9\text{ cm}$ and width $4\text{ cm}$?
questions.explanation: Perimeter $= 9 + 4 + 9 + 4 = 26\text{ cm}$. You must add all four sides.

questions.stem: What is the area of a rectangle $7\text{ cm}$ long and $6\text{ cm}$ wide?
questions.explanation: Area $= \text{length} \times \text{width} = 7 \times 6 = 42\text{ cm}^2$. Area is always in square units.

questions.stem: A triangle has base $8\text{ cm}$ and perpendicular height $5\text{ cm}$. What is its area?
What is the area of a parallelogram with base $10\text{ cm}$ and perpendicular height $3\text{ cm}$?
questions.explanation: Area of a parallelogram $= b \times h = 10 \times 3 = 30\text{ cm}^2$.

questions.stem: A triangle has an area of $24\text{ cm}^2$ and a base of $8\text{ cm}$. What is its perpendicular height?
A square has a perimeter of $36\text{ cm}$. What is the length of one side?
questions.explanation: A square has four equal sides, so side length $= 36 \div 4 = 9\text{ cm}$.

questions.stem: Which unit is most suitable for the area of a classroom floor?
questions.explanation: Area is measured in square units. A classroom floor is large, so square metres are the best choice.

questions.stem: An L-shaped compound figure is made from two rectangles: one $5\text{ cm}$ by $4\text{ cm}$ and another $3\text{ cm}$ by $2\text{ cm}$. What is the total area?
questions.explanation: Area $= (5 \times 4) + (3 \times 2) = 20 + 6 = 26\text{ cm}^2$. Add the areas of the simple parts.

questions.stem: A rectangle has area $48\text{ cm}^2$ and length $8\text{ cm}$. What is its width?
A parallelogram has an area of $28\text{ cm}^2$ and a base of $7\text{ cm}$. What is its perpendicular height?
questions.explanation: Height $= \text{area} \div \text{base} = 28 \div 7 = 4\text{ cm}$. Remember to use perpendicular height.

questions.stem: What is the perimeter of a triangle with sides $7\text{ cm}$, $10\text{ cm}$ and $12\text{ cm}$?
questions.explanation: Perimeter $= 7 + 10 + 12 = 29\text{ cm}$. Add every side once.

questions.stem: A shape is made from a rectangle $8\text{ cm}$ by $5\text{ cm}$ with a triangle on top. The triangle has base $8\text{ cm}$ and height $3\text{ cm}$. What is the total area?
questions.explanation: Rectangle area $= 8 \times 5 = 40\text{ cm}^2$. Triangle area $= \frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 3 = 12\text{ cm}^2$. Total $= 40 + 12 = 52\text{ cm}^2$.

questions.stem: A farmer wants to put fence posts every $5\text{ m}$ around the outside of a rectangular field $50\text{ m}$ by $30\text{ m}$, including the corners. How many posts are needed?
questions.explanation: Perimeter $= 2(50+30) = 160\text{ m}$. Number of posts $= 160 \div 5 = 32$. The spacing divides the perimeter exactly, so posts at every corner and every $5\text{ m}$.

questions.stem: A rectangular wall measures $6\text{ m}$ by $4\text{ m}$. Two identical doors, each $1.5\text{ m}$ by $2\text{ m}$, are not to be painted. What area must be painted?
questions.explanation: Wall area $= 6 \times 4 = 24\text{ m}^2$. Two doors cover $2 \times (1.5 \times 2) = 6\text{ m}^2$. Painted area $= 24 - 6 = 18\text{ m}^2$.
